chunks: And with this chain of transmission, from Yunus, from Mansur ibn Hazim, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Is there anything today that was not in the knowledge of Allah yesterday? He (peace be upon him) replied: No. May Allah disgrace anyone who says this! I said: What about what has happened and what will happen until the Day of Judgment? Is it not in the knowledge of Allah? He (peace be upon him) replied: Yes, even before He created the creation.

key_terms.الْأَمْسِ: Yesterday (referring to the past relative to the present moment of creation)

ai.seo_question: Does God's knowledge change when events happen?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq uses this narration to distinguish between the eternal, unchanging knowledge of Allah and the concept of Al-Bada’ (divine manifestation), clarifying that 'newness' refers to the actualization of events in creation rather than a change in God's essence. By affirming that all occurrences are known prior to creation, the Imam refutes the Mu'tazilite view of static foreknowledge while maintaining divine omniscience. This distinction is pivotal in Shia theology for reconciling predestination with the dynamic nature of divine decree.
